SUBJECT: Arrest of a communist suspect named CHENG TUNG TSIE
(鄭通濟).

REFERENCE: Suppression of communism in the French Concession.
Tseng Fong (正風) Secondary School, Route Prosper
Paris.

At 10.30 p.m. January 6, 1937 Russian Auxiliary Constables
Nos. 20 and 49 and Chinese Policeman No. 617 brought to Central
Station one named CHEN TUNG TSIE (鄭通濟), who was proceeding
in a westerly direction by ricsha along Rue Bourgeat, and who,
when arrested and searched, was found in possession of twelve
books, which he was hiding in a coverlet.

With the assistance of D.S. WRIGHT of the Settlement
Police, Sergeant OUSSAKOVSKY raided No. 37 Tou Foh Li (多福里),
Avenue Foch, the home of the arrested man. This raid, however,
gave no results.

In view of the fact that a piece of paper bearing a
scheme of an organisation project was found and seeming sus-
picious, the individual was detained for further enquiries.

CHENG TUNG TSIE is 25 years of age, a teacher at the
TSENG FONG (正風) Secondary School, Route Prosper Paris,
and is the younger brother of one CHENG TUNG WU (鄭通和),
chief of the Shanghai Secondary School, established by the
Kiangsu Provincial Government (江蘇省立上海中學).

Interviewed, Mr. HOU TSANG SHIH (胡昌時), head of
the Tseng Fong Secondary School, Route Prosper Paris, confirmed
the statement of CHENG TUNG TSIE.

A little later, Mr. CHENG TUNG WU (鄭通和), elder brother
of the arrested man, came to the station and stated that he would
act as a guaranter for the honesty of, and political activities of,
his brother.

There being insufficient proof, and acting in accordance
with instructions, CHENG TUNG TSIE was released and handed over
to his brother. The Chinese Police, however, have been informed
of these suspected activities.

Shanghai, January 7, 1937.

TO THE POLITICAL SECTION OF THE FRENCH POLICE.

Gentlemen,

I have the honour to inform you that my
younger brother TUNG TSLE (通濟 ), a graduate of the
Fu-Tan University, is now a teacher of the Tseng Fong
(正風 ) Secondary School. His ideas and activities
are quite honest and I take all responsibility for them.

Signed and sealed:
CHANG TUNG WU.
Chief of the School.

STATEMENT MADE AT HEADQUARTERS at 9 A.M. JANUARY 7, 1937 BY
CHENG TUNG TSIE (鄭通濟 ). TAKEN BY D.S. J. PERLE.
-------

Q. What are your names, age, profession, place of birth and where
is your home?

A. My name is CHEN TUNG TSIE alias CHEN YAO KUO (鄭耀谷 ), 25,
native of Lukian (Anhwei), residing at 37 Tou Foh Li, (多福里 ),
Avenue Foch, teacher at the Tseng Fong (正風 ) Secondary
School, Route Prosper Paris.

Q. How long have you been in Shanghai?

A. Nine years.

Q. Where were you educated?

A. I was educated at the Shanghai Secondary School, established
by the Kiangsu Provincial Government. My brother is the
Head of this institution. In 1932 I went to the Fu Tan
University, from which I graduated during July 1936. I
remained four months unemployed during which period I lived with
my elder brother. Towards December, thanks to him, I secured
a post as a teacher at the Tseng Fong Secondary School, Route
Prosper Paris. I have never been concerned in politics.

Q. The piece of paper bearing an organisation scheme appears to us
to have at least some political object.

A. During the evening of January 4, 1937 the head of the school
held a meeting of the ten school teachers and requested us to
each form some ideas for the organisation of a military training
scheme for the school. The Shanghai Military Training Committee,
with offices in Nantao - I do not know the exact address -
had asked the Head to take these measures. (The Headmaster
of the School confirms this part of the statement.) I there-
fore prepared this scheme, and perhaps the other teachers did
the same as I did.

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.
Assistance to French Police.

At 12.20a.m. 7-1-37, D.I. Oussakovsky and C.D.C. 307 attached to the Special Branch, French Police brought to the station a male Chinese Zung Tong Ts (曾通達), 25, An-wei, t/teacher, 37/504 Avenue Joch and requested assistance to visit the mentioned address to search for Communistic publications.

Enquiries made by C.D.C. 213 and the undersigned ascertained that the above mentioned person was stopped at 10p.m. 6-1-37 on Route des Soeurs, F.C. by a Police Search Party and when searched was found to have a small quantity of communistic literature in his possession.

The arrested person stated that he was a teacher employed at the Tsung Faung (正風中學) Middle School, on Route Prosper Paris, F.C.

The necessary assistance was rendered, but nothing of an incriminating nature was found amongst his effects.

Enquiries learnt that the arrested person had removed into the Avenue Joch premises on 4-1-37.
